newsitem.title: UK: Commercial Union new sales up 25 pct in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Union new sales up 25 pct in Q1.

text.p: British insurance group Commercial Union Plc said on Wednesday its new life, pensions and investment sales grew 25 percent to 853 million pounds ($1.4 billion) in the first quarter.
The company's single premium sales rose 27 percent to 694 million pounds during the period.
Commercial Union new sales up 25 pct =2
New annual premiums were 28 percent higher at 74 million pounds, and sales of investment products increased 12 percent to 85 million pounds, Commercial Union said.
Commercial Union's shares marked up early gains, rising 10 pence to 650 by 0725 GMT.
"The group has made a very good start to 1997," chief executive John Carter said.
"New business development moved ahead strongly in most of our worldwide businesses, including excellent performances from our newer operations in Italy and Poland," he added in a statement.
In France, new single premium sales fell 16 percent to 357 million pounds in the first quarter compared to a buoyant year-ago period, when sales were boosted by a reduction in interest rates.

Meanwhile, single premium sales in Britain more than trebled to 153 million pounds, reflecting strong sales of Commercial Union's with profits Premier Investment Bond and a 75 percent increase in individual pension sales. ($1 = 0.612 British Pounds)
